Usage: yafs -d device_path -f file_path -{r | w} [-v]
       yafs -d device_path -i [-v]

-v   Activates the verbose mode that will print debug information.
-d   It is used to specify the device that has a FAT file system. On Windows,
     the argument must be the device letter, i.e. "e:". On Unix, the
     argument is the device file, i.e. "/dev/hdb1".

-f   It is used to specify the input or output file. If the option -r is used,
     the program will use this file to store the current file system directory
     tree. If the option -w is used, the program will read the sorted file
     system directory tree from the file.

-o   Optional. When used with -r selects the export format. Supported values
     are "xml" (default) and "json".

-i   With this option, the program only prints some information about the
     device file system. It can't be combined with the -r or -w options.

-r   With this option the program will print the current file system directory
     tree in the file specified with -f option. It can't be combined with the
     -i or -w options.

-w   This option is the only one that modifies the device file system. The
     program will read the sorted file system directory tree from the file
     specified with -f option and then it will change the device file system
     so the files and directories on it have an order equal to the order
     specified in the input file. It can't be combined with the -i or -r
     options.
